answer: A registry models each agent as a vertex in a credential graph; admission needs a bonded stake and attestations from a tiered issuer terrace. Rewards use a per-identity cap and a delta penalty for correlated attestations, so splitting stake across N identities yields no extra reward: each cluster’s score is capped and penalized. Attacker cost is stake plus independent attestations; collusion is detected by clustering. Limitations include issuer capture, privacy loss, and honest correlation.
